category.name: Comparison
category.preferred_workflow: Create deterministic in-memory source documents, optionally write them to temporary files, configure only the CompareOptions members that exist in the installed Aspose.Words version, call Document.Compare with author and timestamp arguments, iterate Document.Revisions to verify and filter changes, accept or reject revisions as required, and finally save the document; always reset MemoryStream.Position before reuse and dispose objects that implement IDisposable.

strict_api_bans: Do not reference Aspose.Words members that are not present in version 26.11.0.
Do not invent comparison options, revision members, or enum values that are absent from the official API.
canonical_patterns: Use Document.Compare with a real author name and comparison timestamp.
Create meaningful differences between local source documents before comparing them.
Inspect and process actual document.Revisions items for filtering, counting, acceptance, or rejection.
nullable_warning_prevention: Initialize all non-nullable reference-type properties to avoid CS8618 warnings.
Guard maybe-null values with explicit null checks before dereferencing them.
Declare locals as nullable when a value may legitimately be null and verify them before use.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: The compiler reports CS0117 errors for properties such as IgnoreCase, IgnoreWhitespace, ShowDeletedContent, DetectMove, DetectMovedParagraphs, and ComparisonTarget.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The code references CompareOptions members that were removed or never existed in the current Aspose.Words release.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Reference only the properties documented for CompareOptions in version 26.11.0, such as IgnoreCaseChanges, IgnoreFormatting, or use reflection to set optional flags when they are available.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Consult the official API reference for the exact property names and guard reflective access with version checks.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: CS1061 errors appear for Revision.GetText, Revision.RevisionDate, Revision.RevisionDateTime, and missing RevisionCollection.Clear.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The code attempts to call members that are not part of the Revision class in the installed library.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Use Revision.ParentNode?.GetText() to obtain affected text and Revision.DateTime for timestamps; do not call Clear on RevisionCollection because it is read-only.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Access only the members listed in the Revision documentation and treat the Revisions collection as immutable.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: CS1674 errors indicate that Document cannot be used in a using statement because it does not implement IDisposable.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The code assumes Document implements IDisposable, which it does not in Aspose.Words.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Create Document instances without a using block and rely on the garbage collector, or call Document.Dispose only if a future version adds it.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Check the type hierarchy before applying the disposable pattern.

common_failure_patterns.pattern: Missing exception types for loading errors
common_failure_patterns.symptom: CS0234 and CS0246 errors show that LoadingException, FileFormatException, and LoadFormatException are not defined.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The code imports exception types that belong to other libraries or older Aspose.Words versions.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Catch the generic Aspose.Words.LoadFormatException or System.IO.IOException as appropriate.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Reference the exception types that appear in the current API documentation.

common_failure_patterns.pattern: Assuming revisions without inspecting the collection
common_failure_patterns.symptom: Logic checks revision counts or types based on hard-coded values rather than enumerating Document.Revisions.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The example code reports expected revision numbers without verifying them.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Iterate Document.Revisions and count or filter actual items to determine the outcome.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Always base decisions on the live Revisions collection.

common_failure_patterns.pattern: Comparing identical documents without introducing differences
common_failure_patterns.symptom: The comparison produces zero revisions even though the task expects changes.
common_failure_patterns.cause: Both source documents contain the same content.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Introduce deterministic differences such as altered text, formatting, or structural changes before calling Compare.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Create sample inputs that deliberately differ in the aspect under test.

narrative.overview: The Comparison category demonstrates how to use Aspose.Words native document-comparison APIs to detect, process, and report revisions across a variety of document types. Verified examples cover author attribution, case-insensitive comparison, whitespace-ignoring comparison, moved-paragraph detection, revision-target selection, deleted-content retention, orientation changes, chart revisions, revision enumeration, and table-cell formatting analysis.
narrative.purpose: An AI coding agent should generate correct, self-contained C# snippets that create sample source documents, configure supported CompareOptions, invoke Document.Compare, inspect the Document.Revisions collection, and persist the result while respecting nullability and resource-management guidelines.
validation_priorities: Ensure that the compiled snippet uses only members that exist in Aspose.Words 26.11.0 and that revision handling is performed through the Document.Revisions collection.
maintenance_notes: Update the example code whenever a new Aspose.Words release changes the CompareOptions or Revision API surface.
